title: EFC — AI-Augmented Scientific Workflow Framework
description: Defines a structured framework for integrating large language models into scientific workflows while preserving human control, accountability, and reproducibility. It formalizes four core mechanisms—Question Architecture (QA), Entropy Navigation (EN), Reflective Scaffolding (RS), and Strict Separation of Roles (SR)—to ensure transparent provenance, machine-readable intent, entropy-guided exploration, and external grounding of AI reflections. The work aligns with FAIR principles and emphasizes a human validation gate for all scientific claims.

key_results.main_finding: The paper formalizes a human-governed AI workflow centered on QA, EN, RS, and SR to deliver reproducible, traceable, and accountable AI-assisted research.

kill_criteria: KC1: Reproducibility failure — given a fixed QA object, fixed prompts, seeds, and environment, repeated pipeline runs produce non-identical artifacts (checksum mismatch) beyond predefined tolerances.

KC2: RS grounding failure — for a benchmark set of tasks with known external formal models (e.g., causal diagrams or state machines), Reflective Scaffolding cannot map AI claims to external constraints with ≥95% coverage and ≤5% contradiction rate across N trials.
KC3: Provenance gap — mandatory artifacts (version history, reflective logs, and machine-readable metadata) are missing or unverifiable for >1% of outputs over a validated run set.
KC4: Role leakage — audit shows AI-generated interpretive conclusions included in final claims without passing the documented human validation gate in ≥1% of evaluated cases.

KC5: EN inefficacy — on pre-registered literature discovery or hypothesis expansion benchmarks, Entropy Navigation does not outperform random/baseline heuristic search on agreed novelty/precision metrics by a statistically significant margin.
KC6: QA breakdown — the Question Architecture cannot consistently produce machine-readable question objects that pass schema validation in ≥99% of attempts on a standardized test suite.
